title: Show opening and introduction of Mary Collins and her book
summary: Host opens Speaking of Blues, plays a Little Brother Montgomery record, and introduces Mrs. Lee Collins and her book about trumpeter Lee Collins.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Opening the interview: introductions, date and place

blocks.x: The show is called Speaking of Blues. And tonight we have a special guest on the show. A lady whose name is Mary.
Little Brother recorded a song and it was I think in 1952. It had something to do with the Victory Club.

This was one Sunday morning boy. And old Papa Ammons was over there, Abbot, before he passed. Boy you talking about some fun we had. He and Papa Yassid, they double headed the piano boy. And we danced there that morning till 9, 10 o'clock. That reminds me of Bigfoot Clows at the Victory Club. You ever heard Bigfoot Clows play? He and Sweet Frank Williams. Along about 3 or 4 o'clock in the morning, Milt Moore and Jack Teagarden came by. I run into a little girl with a green dress on and some red stocket. Boy that little chick was gone. She was a solid Senator. I run into a little girl with a green dress on and some red stocking for her. Boy, that little chick was gone. She was a solid sender. Boy, she really couldn't boogie.

A classic by Little Brother Montgomery, to say the least. And I'd like to remind you, this is WLDC at Loyola University, and we're in New Orleans. And we're doing an interview with Mrs. Lee Collins, whose husband is Trumpeter Lee Collins. And she has written a book, and it's entitled, Oh, Didn't He Ramble? And we're trying to talk about Lee and something about the book and get into a few things about it. What inspired you to write a book about your husband? Well, Lee.
